title: Exact Markovian Dissipation Requires Singular Energy Resources
abstract: The Gorini--Kossakowski--Lindblad--Sudarshan (GKLS) equation describes irreversible quantum dynamical semigroups. We show that this description cannot be exact under physically regular energy conditions. We prove that the open-system survival probability under physically regular energy conditions has sublinear decay, whereas any dissipative GKLS semigroup has a linear short-time decay. Hence exact Markovian dissipation requires singular energy resources: an unbounded-below total Hamiltonian or infinite initial energy, and a divergent interaction-energy moment. Therefore, a dissipative time-independent GKLS equation should be regarded as an effective description rather than the exact reduced dynamics of a Hamiltonian dilation satisfying physically regular energy conditions.
summary: The paper proves that standard, physically regular Hamiltonian descriptions cannot exactly reproduce the linear short-time decay characteristic of Markovian dissipation described by the GKLS equation. This forces the conclusion that such dissipative processes must be understood as effective approximations rather than exact reduced dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether irreversible quantum dissipation, described by the GKLS equation, can be exactly modeled as the reduced dynamics of a physically regular Hamiltonian dilation.
main_result: Exact Markovian dissipation requires singular energy resources (e.g., unbounded Hamiltonians), implying that such dissipative processes must be treated as effective descriptions rather than exact reductions from standard physical Hamiltonians.
method: The authors compare the short-time decay of the survival probability ($\ell(t)$) predicted by physically regular Hamiltonian evolutions ($o(t)$ or $O(t^2)$) against the linear initial decay ($\Gamma t$) characteristic of non-unitary GKLS semigroups.
model_or_system: The system involves open quantum dynamics governed by the Gorini–Kossakowski–Lindblad–Sudarshan (GKLS) equation. The analysis contrasts this with unitary evolution generated by a total Hamiltonian $H = H_S + H_E + H_{int}$ acting on an environment.
key_observables: Survival probability loss ($\ell(t)$), and the linear decay coefficient $\Gamma$ derived from the GKLS generator.
important_parameters: The regularity conditions, specifically requiring the total Hamiltonian to be bounded below or having finite short-time interaction energy moments.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes 'physically regular energy conditions' (e.g., lower bound on $H$ or finite second moment of $H_{int}$).
